about: Single source of truth for every visual asset. Prompt files in assets/prompts/ are GENERATED from this file by tools/assets/build-prompts.mjs — edit here, then run `npm run assets:prompts`.
surfaceReference: assets/reference/surface-reference.png — the team's design reference for the SURFACE (low cream-and-grey habitat with a central airlock dome and lit windows, dish, lattice radio tower with a red beacon, boxy yellow-white rover, red mountains, violet-pink dusty sky). Every surface asset is built on it. SCENARIO.md still wins where they differ: the reference sky is dusk, the scenario says dusty orange daytime, so the sky is orange-pink fading to violet; the scenario antenna is BENT.
scenario: Rebuilt for SCENARIO.md (Ares-1, Jezero Crater, ASTRA 6.7, builder drones). Every subject below is taken from SCENARIO sections 2-5; anything the scenario does not describe is marked PROPOSAL in `notes`.

statuses.awaiting-generation: Prompt is ready. No image exists yet.
statuses.awaiting-lore: Cannot be specified properly until the scenario says more.
statuses.received: Raw image is in assets/incoming/, not yet processed.
statuses.processed: Cleaned, sliced and saved under assets/art/, not yet wired into the game.
statuses.integrated: Loaded and drawn by the game.
statuses.final: Integrated, checked on screen, approved by the team.
statuses.procedural-standin: Drawn by code as a labelled placeholder (SCENARIO section 6, rule 3). Never final art.

world.note: World units come from SCENARIO section 4 (1920 x 3200, ground at Y 1050). The scale of 5 units per art pixel is a PROPOSAL: every coordinate in the scenario divides by 5. The game draws at the logical size and scales up by a whole number.

canvas.note: The window onto the world is 1920 x 1080 units = 384 x 216 art pixels, scaled x5 to 1920x1080 (x2 = 768x432 for small screens).

grid.note: Module 600 x 270 units = 120 x 54 px; shaft 120 x 270 = 24 x 54 px; an astronaut is 175 units = 35 px tall. All PROPOSALS following from 5 units per pixel.

common.styleRules: Pixel art with crisp, un-blurred pixels. Flat orthographic side view (like an ant farm): no perspective, no vanishing point. A limited palette of about 24 colours shared by the whole game. One-pixel dark outline on characters and props, none on terrain. Light comes from the upper left. Warm Martian oranges, rusts and butterscotch for the world; cream and white for hulls; cyan (#00E5FF) and amber (#FFB000) for ASTRA and electronics; Martian Orange #FF6B35 only for highlights. Friendly and tidy for children aged 7-12: rounded corners, no gore, no frightening shapes.
common.avoid: No text or letters inside the image (the game draws all text), no watermarks, no anti-aliased gradients, no photorealism, no 3D rendering, no perspective, no extra characters unless asked.

assets.title: Style anchor — Ares-1 in one picture
assets.purpose: Defines the look of the entire game. Every other asset is generated with this image attached as the style reference. Not used in the game itself (it may become the title screen).
assets.perspective: Side view, flat orthographic cutaway (like an ant farm).
assets.background: opaque
assets.subject: The whole Mars base Ares-1 in Jezero Crater as one tall cross-section through the ground. TOP FIFTH, sky and mountains: a dusty orange-pink Martian sky fading to violet at the top, with layers of red-brown crater-rim mountains and a violet haze, exactly in the look of the attached SURFACE REFERENCE image. THE GROUND LINE sits about a third of the way down. Standing on it, left to right: a few solar panels thickly covered in rust-coloured dust; a long low cream-and-grey surface habitat with rounded roofs, a central AIRLOCK DOME with a round hatch and lit orange windows (designed like the habitat in the reference); the bent antenna: a tall lattice radio tower with a dish on it, BENT and crooked and dusty, with a dark beacon on top; an empty landing pad; a heap of loose regolith with two small robot drones half-buried in it, dormant, with dark dead lights. BELOW THE GROUND, a thick layer of reddish soil with horizontal strata and small stones, then the base in a 2 by 4 grid of rooms with a vertical ladder shaft between the two wings. LEFT WING, finished and cosy, lit with warm yellow ceiling light, top to bottom: a Bedroom with bunk beds; a Dining Room with a table, stools and an exercise bike; a Water and Air Life Support room with tanks, pipes and a glowing teal oxygen machine; the fourth room below is empty rock. RIGHT WING, unfinished and dark: bare dark-steel frames, girders and scaffolding standing in loose sand with no walls and no lights, top to bottom: a Workshop frame; a Research and Comms Lab frame with a dish base; a Battery and Heating frame with empty battery shelves; a Rover Garage frame in which a small builder drone (a round body, four little arms, a solar panel on top) sits motionless with a single blinking red LED. One small astronaut in a cream jumpsuit, helmet off, stands in the Bedroom. Under the rooms, more soil and bedrock.
assets.layout: One full tall scene edge to edge. Sky and surface in the top 35%, soil band, then the rooms on a regular grid (2 columns of 4 rows, shaft in the middle), soil and bedrock at the bottom.
assets.notes: PROVISIONAL: candidate v3 (assets/incoming/style.anchor.v3.png, copied to style.anchor.png) is used as the reference while the team has not confirmed it; candidates v1 and v2 are kept. If the team picks another, every generated asset must be redone. Generate several candidates and choose ONE together. Everything else copies its palette, pixel size, outline and lighting, so this choice is the important one. The tall ratio matches the 1920 x 3200 world; the game itself only ever shows a 16:9 window of it.

assets.title: Martian sky and Jezero Crater rim
assets.purpose: The top zone of the world (Y 0 to 1050): what the player sees during the descent and at the surface.
assets.generate: 16:9 (e.g. 1920x1080); crop to the right proportions afterwards
assets.background: opaque
assets.subject: A dusty Martian sky in the colours of the attached SURFACE REFERENCE image: warm orange-pink near the horizon, fading through dusty rose to violet at the top, with faint thin cloud streaks and a small pale sun. Two or three layers of distant jagged red-brown crater-rim mountains and mesas along the bottom edge, with a violet haze between the layers. The very bottom edge is flat, so the ground can be placed over it. No buildings.
assets.layout: One wide scene. Mountains only in the bottom 20%. The left and right edges must match so it can scroll sideways without a seam.
assets.notes: SCENARIO section 4: 'dusty orange Martian sky, distant Jezero Crater mountains'. The reference is a dusk sky; the scenario says dusty orange, so it is orange-pink fading to violet (daylight is needed for solar power). Used behind the lander during the descent (camera Y 400).

assets.title: Martian soil and sand — tile set
assets.purpose: Everything around and between the rooms: ground surface, soil under the ground line, rock, and the loose sand the unfinished right wing stands in.

frames.order: row 1: surface top with pebbles x3, surface top with a small rock | row 2: loose reddish regolith fill x4 (subtle strata) | row 3: compacted darker soil x2, soil with embedded stones x2 | row 4: bedrock x2, pale blue-white ice pocket in soil x2 | row 5: loose pale sand for the unfinished wing x4

assets.background: opaque
assets.subject: Seamless ground tiles for a cross-section of Martian soil. Rust and orange-brown regolith with faint horizontal layers, getting darker and more violet with depth. Small stones and a few larger rocks. Ice pockets are pale blue-white crystals surrounded by soil. Row 5 is lighter, finer, drifted sand. Each tile must tile seamlessly with the others in its row, left-right.
assets.layout: A strict grid of 4 columns x 5 rows of equal square tiles with no gaps and no borders between them.
assets.notes: SCENARIO section 4: 'dark steel frames in sand' (right wing) and 'red Martian soil layers' (the camera pan slices through them).

assets.subject: A long, low surface habitat designed exactly like the one in the attached SURFACE REFERENCE image: cream-and-grey modules with rounded roofs, a larger central AIRLOCK DOME with a round hatch door, a smaller dome on each side, rows of small lit orange-yellow windows, a ramp, little vents and pipes, a thin layer of rust-coloured dust on the roofs and at the foot. assets.title: Astronaut, indoor jumpsuit — sprite sheet
assets.purpose: The crew inside the base: every indoor activity of the simulation (idle, walk, work, eat, sleep, exercise, climb), plus the helmet-off moment of the cutscene.
assets.perspective: Side view, character facing right. The game mirrors it for facing left.

frames.order: row 1: idle x2, walk x4 | row 2: walk x2 (completing the 6-frame cycle), work standing at a console x4 | row 3: sitting and eating x2, sleeping lying down x2, exercising on a bike x2 | row 4: climbing a ladder seen from the side x4, taking the helmet off x2

assets.background: transparent, or solid #FF00FF if transparency is not available
assets.subject: One friendly astronaut in a simple short-sleeved cream jumpsuit and soft boots, no helmet, short hair, neutral skin tone, about 35 pixels tall inside a 40x44 cell. The collar, shoulder stripe and belt are flat pure cyan #00FFFF (this colour is replaced in the game with each crew member's colour, so it must be flat and used nowhere else). Big readable head, simple dot eyes. Same character, same proportions and same size in every cell. The two helmet-off frames show the same jumpsuit with a white helmet being lifted off, then held under the arm.
assets.layout: A sprite sheet: a strict grid of 6 columns x 4 rows of equal cells. One pose per cell, centred horizontally, feet on the same baseline 2 pixels above the bottom of the cell (the sleeping pose lies on that baseline). Nothing crosses a cell border.
assets.notes: Simulation activities: sleep, walk, work, meal, exercise, free, shelter, recover. 'free', 'shelter' and 'recover' reuse idle and sitting. SCENARIO section 4: at 20.0 s the astronaut exits the airlock and removes the helmet. How many people arrive and who they are is an open question (docs/LEVELS.md, point 7), so for now one design recoloured per person.

assets.subject: A small friendly builder robot: a rounded squat orange-and-white body about 22 pixels wide, a solar panel on its back, four short jointed arms with tool tips, two small caterpillar tracks, one round camera 'eye' and a single status LED on top. Dormant: slumped, the eye dark, the LED red. Awake: upright, the eye glowing cyan, the LED green. Same robot, same proportions in every cell.

assets.notes: SCENARIO section 4: 'Drone #01 with a blinking red LED'; the LED blinks at 1 Hz from 22.0 s. Awake drones help build by daylight only (they are solar powered) - hence the night frames. Fallback label in code: DRONE_01. Drone shape is a PROPOSAL.

assets.title: ASTRA 6.7 — animated avatar
assets.purpose: The guide's portrait in the ASTRA panel (left side of the screen). Animates while she speaks; the mood prop changes her colours and expression.
assets.perspective: Front view, centred, on a plain dark panel-coloured background.

frames.order: row 1 (calm, cyan): idle x2, speaking x2 | row 2: cheerful (amber-cyan, bright) | curious (head tilt, ring lifted) | alert (amber-orange, ring flashing) | proud (soft glow)

assets.background: transparent, or solid #FF00FF if transparency is not available
assets.subject: A friendly station AI shown as a glowing geometric core: a round cyan-and-amber ring with a bright centre, two thin waveform lines either side that move when she speaks, and a few small orbiting dots. No face, no human features, no scary red eye. Calm: cyan. Cheerful: warm amber with a little sparkle. Curious: the ring tilted. Alert: amber-orange with a flashing ring. Clean, soft and trustworthy.
assets.layout: A strict grid of 4 columns x 2 rows of equal cells. The core centred in each cell.
assets.notes: SCENARIO section 2: 'animated holographic/digital avatar portrait (cyan/amber waveforms or friendly geometric AI core that animates while speaking)'. Mood values (calm, cheerful, curious, alert) are a PROPOSAL; 'proud' is spare.

assets.subject: Four unfinished underground rooms. Each is a skeleton of dark blue-grey steel girders, columns and scaffolding, standing in loose pale sand on a sand floor, with no walls, no lights, a few cables hanging, a stack of unopened crates and a half-built wall panel. Each has a faint hint of what it will become: a bare workbench frame (Workshop); an empty rack and a dish base (Lab); empty battery shelves and a heater pipe (Battery & Heating); wide floor markings and a ramp (Rover Garage). The Garage frame holds a motionless builder drone with one small red light.
assets.layout: A strict grid of 2 columns x 2 rows of equal cells. No borders between cells. The right edge of each cell is a door opening.
assets.notes: SCENARIO section 4: 'Right Wing (Unfinished, dark steel frames in sand)'. Build progress (0-100%) is shown by the game fading this frame into module.finished.
